Bill.BriefDescription: Protecting the water quality in Hood Canal.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to protecting Hood Canal by removing nitrates andphosphates from onsite sewage disposal systems and wastewatertreatment plants; amending RCW 70.118B.040; adding a new section tochapter 90.88 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 70.118 RCW; addinga new section to chapter 70.118A RCW; and adding a new section tochapter 90.48 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.88 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) In aquatic rehabilitation zone one, any new or retrofitted onsite sewage disposal systems installed after July 1, 2009, may notdischarge to ground or surface waters more than twenty milligrams perliter of total nitrogen. In aquatic rehabilitation zone one, any newor retrofitted wastewater treatment system installed after July 1,2009, must use all known, available, and reasonable methods of nitrogenremoval. (2) By December 1, 2008, the department of health and thedepartment of ecology shall jointly report to the legislature regarding p. 1 SHB 3227the impact of removing phosphates from the discharge of onsite sewagedisposal systems and wastewater treatment systems in aquaticrehabilitation zone one.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.118 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW 90.88.010,any new or retrofitted onsite sewage disposal system installed afterJuly 1, 2009, may not discharge to ground or surface waters more thantwenty milligrams per liter of total nitrogen.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.118ARCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW 90.88.010,any new or retrofitted onsite sewage disposal system installed afterJuly 1, 2009, may not discharge to ground or surface waters more thantwenty milligrams per liter of total nitrogen.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 70.118B.040 and 2007 c 343 s 5 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) For the protection of human health and the environment, thesecretary shall adopt rules for the comprehensive regulation of largeonsite sewage systems, which includes, but is not limited to, thesiting, design, construction, installation, maintenance, repair, andpermitting of the systems. (2) In adopting the rules, the secretary shall, in consultationwith the department of ecology, require that large onsite sewagesystems comply with the applicable sections of chapter 90.48 RCWregarding control and prevention of pollution of waters of the state,including but not limited to: (a) Surface and groundwater standards established under RCW90.48.035; and (b) Those provisions requiring all known, available, and reasonablemethods of treatment. (3) In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW90.88.010, any new or retrofitted large onsite sewage disposal systeminstalled after July 1, 2009, may not discharge to ground or surfacewaters more than twenty milligrams per liter of total nitrogen. SHB 3227 p. 2 (4) In adopting the rules, the secretary shall ensure thatrequirements for large onsite sewage systems are consistent with therequirements of any comprehensive plans or development regulationsadopted under chapter 36.70A RCW or any other applicable comprehensiveplan, land use plan, or development regulation adopted by a city, town,or county.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.48 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW 90.88.010,any new or retrofitted wastewater treatment system installed after July1, 2009, must use all known, available, and reasonable methods ofnitrogen removal.
